title: IMD warns of flash flood risk across central India as monsoon intensifies - businessupturn.com
full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a low to moderate flash flood risk warning for several districts across Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha and Odisha, cautioning that persistent heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours could lead to surface runoff, waterlogging and localized flooding in vulnerable areas. The advisory remains valid until 11:30 a.m. on July 30, with authorities urged to closely monitor low-lying regions and flood-prone watersheds.
The warning comes as the southwest monsoon regains strength over central and northwest India after an uneven start to the season. According to the IMD, saturated soil conditions combined with fresh spells of heavy rainfall could increase the likelihood of flash floods, particularly in districts that have already received significant precipitation in recent days. The weather agency advised residents in vulnerable areas to remain alert and follow instructions issued by local authorities.
Districts under flash flood watch
The IMD's Flash Flood Guidance bulletin covers multiple districts in Chhattisgarh, including Raipur, Durg, Bastar, Dantewada, Bijapur, Kanker, Rajnandgaon, Mahasamund, Baloda Bazar, Balod, Kabirdham, Dhamtari, Gariaband, Janjgir-Champa, Kondagaon, Korea, Narayanpur and Raigarh.
In east Madhya Pradesh, districts including Jabalpur, Mandla, Balaghat, Chhindwara, Dindori, Katni, Damoh, Sagar, Narsinghpur, Singrauli, Tikamgarh, Niwari and Anuppur have also been placed under the advisory.
The weather office issued similar warnings for Nagpur, Wardha, Chandrapur, Gadchiroli, Gondia and Bhandara in Vidarbha, along with several districts across Odisha, including Baleshwar, Bhadrak, Kendujhar, Sundargarh, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Mayurbhanj, Dhenkanal, Bargarh and Angul, among others.
Heavy rain to continue across large parts of India
The IMD said an active monsoon phase is likely to persist over central and northwest India through the first week of August.
The department has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over west Madhya Pradesh on July 30 and Gujarat on July 31, while Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are expected to witness widespread rainfall from July 30 to August 3.
Similar weather conditions are forecast over Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi during July 30–31 and again on August 2–3. East and west Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha are also expected to receive widespread rainfall over the coming days.
The IMD has additionally forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30–50 kmph over parts of Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha.
Delhi-NCR likely to remain wet
Heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms lashed parts of Delhi-NCR over the past day, disrupting traffic and causing waterlogging in several localities. According to the IMD, intermittent rainfall is likely to continue in the region until July 31, with occasional thunderstorms.
Extremely heavy rainfall recorded
In its latest weather bulletin, the IMD said Odisha and Uttarakhand recorded extremely heavy rainfall during the past 24 hours. Very heavy rainfall was reported from Jharkhand, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, east Madhya Pradesh, Konkan and Goa, and Madhya Maharashtra, while heavy rainfall occurred across parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Assam, Telangana and Karnataka.
The department has advised state administrations to monitor vulnerable watersheds, drainage systems and low-lying settlements as continued rainfall could result in localized flooding and transport disruptions.
With the monsoon expected to remain active over the next several days, meteorologists say rainfall may help offset earlier seasonal deficits in some regions but could simultaneously increase flood risks where the ground is already saturated.
